question: From which island did DRDO conduct the 'Pralay' missile tests in July 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island**, formerly known as Wheeler Island, is a prominent missile testing facility located off the coast of Odisha in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** conducted the test for the **'Pralay' missile** from this island in July 2025.
 
• 'Pralay' is a **short-range surface-to-surface tactical missile** developed by the DRDO, designed for quick deployment during conflicts. It is capable of carrying both conventional and nuclear warheads.
 
• The successful test of the 'Pralay' missile highlights India's advancements in **defense technology** and strengthens its tactical strike capabilities.
 
• The island was renamed in honor of **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam**, India's Missile Man and the 11th President of India, recognizing his immense contribution to India's missile and space programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island:**

 
 
• Located approximately 10 kilometers off the Odisha coast, near Chandipur.
 
• Serves as a **dedicated missile test facility** for India's defense programs, managed by the DRDO.
 
• The island is equipped with state-of-the-art tracking systems, radars, and telemetry stations to monitor missile tests.
 
 
 
• **'Pralay' Missile:**
 
 
• A highly maneuverable, short-range ballistic missile with a range of **150–500 kilometers**.
 
• Developed to strike enemy targets with precision, it can carry a payload of **up to 1,000 kilograms**.
 
• Can operate in all weather conditions and is designed to evade interception systems.
 
• Strengthens India's tactical strike capabilities, complementing other missile systems like BrahMos and Agni.
 
 
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• India's premier agency for defense research and development, under the Ministry of Defence.
 
• Established in **1958**, DRDO has played a vital role in developing indigenous defense technologies, including missiles, aircraft, and radar systems.
 
• Other notable missile programs by DRDO include **Agni, Akash, Nag, and BrahMos**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Missile Tests:**
 
 
• Enhances national security by demonstrating the capability to deter potential threats.
 
• Validates the performance and reliability of missile systems under real-world conditions.
 
• Contributes to India's self-reliance in defense technology and reduces dependency on foreign imports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Nicobar Islands:** Located in the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago, these islands are primarily known for their biodiversity and strategic location but are not used for missile tests.
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:** An archipelago off the southwestern coast of India, primarily known for its tourism and maritime significance. No missile tests are conducted here.
 
• **Andaman Islands:** Part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. While they hold strategic importance for India's defense, missile tests are not conducted here.
 
 
 
• The successful test of 'Pralay' from Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island symbolizes India's growing capabilities in **indigenous defense technology**.
 
• Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island continues to be a key site for India's missile development and testing programs, contributing to the nation's security and technological advancements.
